title: Knowledge Check 5: Lessons 21–25
description: Fifteen questions pooled from Lessons 21–25: OmniScripts · Integration Procedures. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: Which is an OmniScript best practice?
options: Modular child scripts, consistent naming, debug-mode testing
questions.explanation: Best practices favor modularity, naming, and debug testing.

questions.question: Where should heavy multi-system orchestration live?
options: In an Integration Procedure called by the script
questions.explanation: IPs handle orchestration; OmniScripts stay lean.

questions.question: Which tool inspects an OmniScript's data JSON during development?
questions.explanation: Debug mode exposes the JSON and element execution for troubleshooting.

questions.question: What is an Integration Procedure?
options: A declarative server-side process executing multiple actions in one call
questions.explanation: IPs orchestrate multiple actions server-side in a single transaction.

questions.question: Why use an IP instead of multiple callouts from a FlexCard?
options: One server call executes the orchestration. Fewer round trips, consistent handling
questions.explanation: IPs consolidate orchestration into one server call.

questions.question: Which order reflects a typical IP flow?
options: Extract → Transform → External call → Load → Respond
questions.explanation: IPs flow data forward: extract, transform, integrate, persist, respond.

questions.question: Which action returns data from an IP to its caller?
questions.explanation: The Response Action defines what the IP returns.

questions.question: An IP must call a REST API using a Named Credential. Which action?
questions.explanation: HTTP Actions make REST callouts; Named Credentials carry auth.

questions.question: Which action invokes another Integration Procedure?
questions.explanation: Sub-IP actions compose IPs for modular orchestration.

questions.question: An IP should call a credit-check API only for amounts over a threshold. What controls this?
options: Conditional logic on the amount JSON path
questions.explanation: Conditionals gate actions based on data values.

questions.question: How does an IP process a list of line items one at a time?
options: A loop over the line items array
questions.explanation: Loops iterate arrays so per-item actions can run.

questions.question: Which IP capability chooses between different action paths for different inputs?
questions.explanation: Branching routes execution based on input state.

questions.question: A long-running process exceeds synchronous transaction limits. What's the right pattern?
options: Chainable IPs splitting work into multiple transactions
questions.explanation: Chainable IPs break long processes into separate transactions.

questions.question: What distinguishes a chainable IP's execution model?
options: Each link runs asynchronously in its own transaction
It runs synchronously with everything else
questions.explanation: Chainable links execute in fresh transactions, keeping each within limits.

questions.question: Which scenario best suits chaining?
options: Long-running multi-step processing that exceeds synchronous limits
questions.explanation: Chaining fits long processes that would blow synchronous limits.
